claims: The Social Security Administration (SSA) warns of a surge in scams where impersonators threaten to suspend Social Security numbers (SSN) to steal money or personal information.
Demands for immediate payment via gift cards, crypto, or wire transfers are key red flags.
Claims of problems with your SSN are key red flags.
Scammers pretend to be SSA or Office of the Inspector General (OIG) agents.
Scammers threaten arrest or legal action for fake issues with your account.
Scammers send phishing emails/texts with links claiming to be "Claim Benefits!".
Scammers send phishing emails/texts with links claiming that your account is suspended.
Scammers use fabricated letters or emails to gather your personal information and redirect benefits.
The SSA will never threaten you, demand immediate payment, or ask for credit card numbers over the phone.
The SSA will generally send a letter if there is a real issue with your account.
